explained.tdh.how.meta.title: How TDH is calculated
explained.tdh.how.meta.description: Time, rarity, collections and you: the TDH v1.4 rules, each with a model you can move.
explained.tdh.how.title: How TDH is calculated
explained.tdh.how.lede: Four ideas, each with a model you can move: time, rarity, collections and you, all running the TDH v1.4 rules in your browser on the real Meme editions.
explained.tdh.how.parts.label: The four parts
explained.tdh.how.parts.a.title: Time
explained.tdh.how.parts.a.line: A day counts only when it is whole.
explained.tdh.how.parts.b.title: Rarity
explained.tdh.how.parts.b.line: Rarer cards count more per copy.
explained.tdh.how.parts.c.title: Collections
explained.tdh.how.parts.d.title: You
explained.tdh.how.parts.d.line: Up to four wallets count as one.
explained.tdh.how.a.title: A day counts only when it is whole.
explained.tdh.how.a.body: Once a day TDH takes a snapshot of Ethereum: the last block before {midnight}. A result is dated by its snapshot and counts the day before it. A copy adds one day for every whole {hours} hours it has been held at that snapshot.
explained.tdh.how.firstday.label: A card ages
explained.tdh.how.firstday.question: When does a copy start to count?
explained.tdh.how.firstday.guess: a copy arrives at {time} on {date}. Which result counts its first whole day?
explained.tdh.how.firstday.answer: {right}. The snapshot of {early} finds one minute; the snapshot of {right} finds {hours} hours and one minute. Two minutes later, at {later}, it would be {after}.
explained.tdh.how.firstday.aria: A timeline of four daily snapshots, the copy's arrival and the time it is held. {say}
explained.tdh.how.firstday.sayFirst: The result dated {date} counts its first whole day ({held} held).
explained.tdh.how.firstday.sayBefore: The one before found {held}: not a whole day.
explained.tdh.how.firstday.saySold: It left before a whole day: no result ever counts it, and the buyer starts from zero.
explained.tdh.how.firstday.sayNone: No result in this window counts it yet.
explained.tdh.how.firstday.ruleT: T = {day} × N, the snapshot of cycle N
explained.tdh.how.firstday.ruleSource: P26 §4.1, §4.3 · whole days, never parts of one
explained.tdh.how.cards.label: Which cards count
explained.tdh.how.cards.lead: A card counts once its first mint is a whole day old.
explained.tdh.how.cards.example: {card} was first minted on {date} at {time}, so it counts from the result dated {from}.
explained.tdh.how.cards.tail: Meme cards, 6529 Gradients and NextGen tokens count; nothing else does.
explained.tdh.how.moves.label: Sales and moves
explained.tdh.how.moves.body: Every copy remembers when it arrived. A sale takes the sold copy's days with it, and when you sell one of several copies, the one you received last goes first. A move between your own linked wallets keeps its age: {link}.
explained.tdh.how.netting.label: Inside one transaction
explained.tdh.how.netting.question: If a copy leaves and comes back in one transaction, did it ever leave?
explained.tdh.how.netting.netSay: Nothing moved, so nothing is replayed.
explained.tdh.how.netting.stepsSay: Counted step by step, the copy leaves A and comes back new.
explained.tdh.how.netting.sayNet: TDH v1.4 replays each transaction's net movement only, so A's copy keeps its {days} days.
explained.tdh.how.netting.saySteps: the copy would restart at zero. TDH nets each transaction first (D131), so this does not happen.
explained.tdh.how.netting.hOne: A sends one copy of Meme #{m1} to C, and someone mints {n} copies of Meme #{m1} to X and burns them in the same transaction.
explained.tdh.how.netting.hTwo: Every net movement is the same with or without the mint and burn, so every stack is the same. But the card's minted count reads the logged steps: minted rises from {mintedBefore} to {mintedAfter}, H from {hBefore} to {hAfter}, the rate of Meme #{m2} from {rateBefore} to {rateAfter}, and B's TDH from {bBefore} to {bAfter}.
explained.tdh.how.netting.sayH: Netting is proved for the holding stacks only. A mint and its burn inside one transaction can still change other holders' TDH (counterexample H, a small constructed input). The pages say so wherever netting is claimed.
explained.tdh.how.netting.break: mint and burn in one transaction
explained.tdh.how.b.title: Rarer cards count more per copy, and every card adds about the same.
explained.tdh.how.b.body: A card's rate is {H} divided by its edition: {H} is FirstGM's edition, the largest, so FirstGM's rate is {rateFirstGM} and a {cap}-copy card's is {rate310}. Below {threshold} copies minted, a card counts as if it had its claim's limit, up to {cap}, because every release is topped up to {cap}. No edition goes below {threshold}: that threshold is one of The Memes' two absolutes.
explained.tdh.how.rates.label: The rate and the edition floor
explained.tdh.how.rates.question: Why does a rare card earn more per copy, yet every card adds about the same?
explained.tdh.how.rates.sayFloor: Below {threshold} copies a card counts at its claim limit, up to {cap}, because the release tops it up to {cap}. Each copy adds {rate} a day; all {E} copies together add {area} a day, about the same as every other card.
explained.tdh.how.rates.say: each copy adds {rate} a day; all {E} copies together add {area} a day, about the same as every other card.
explained.tdh.how.rates.ruleSource: P26 §5.2, §8.1. A floor applies only below {threshold} minted; the {threshold} is locked (D89). Exact half cents round as P26 §8.1 says: see the {link}.
explained.tdh.how.base.label: Base TDH
explained.tdh.how.base.body: Each card's base TDH is its copies × whole days × rate, rounded to a whole number once per card in each wallet. Two copies of a {cap}-copy card held {days} days add {sum}, rounded to {rounded}. That rounding is why a move between your own linked wallets can change your total by a unit or two.
explained.tdh.how.c.title: One boost multiplies everything you hold.
explained.tdh.how.c.body: Each complete season adds {season}, once the next season has begun. A full set takes every complete season, plus a little for each further set. Genesis (#1 to #3) and Nakamoto (#4) add {single} each while the first season is not complete. Each 6529 Gradient adds {gradient}, up to {max}. Today's highest boost is about {todayMax}; the rule's ceiling is about {ceiling}, once season {last} is complete.
explained.tdh.how.boost.label: The boost ladder
explained.tdh.how.boost.question: What multiplies everything a collector holds, and where does it stop?
explained.tdh.how.boost.sayGrad: Gradients add {gradient} each, up to {max}; this one is a plain copy that earns its own rate.
explained.tdh.how.boost.saySets: A full set takes every complete season ({count} today), plus a little for each further set, never more than about {extra} in all.
explained.tdh.how.boost.saySingles: Genesis (#1 to #3) and Nakamoto (#4) count only while the first season is not complete.
explained.tdh.how.boost.say: One boost multiplies everything you hold. The newest season counts once the next one begins.
explained.tdh.how.d.title: Up to four wallets count as one collector.
explained.tdh.how.d.body: Wallets linked both ways become one identity. Their copies add up, the boost is computed once on everything they hold together, and copies moved between them keep their age. Your final TDH is each card's base times that one boost, rounded per card.
explained.tdh.how.d.link: How to link them, and why a number changes
explained.tdh.how.identity.sayLinked: Linked, A and B together hold all {count} cards of season {season}, so one boost of {boost} applies to every card: {tdh} TDH.
explained.tdh.how.identity.sayApart: Apart, neither wallet completes the season, so neither has a boost: {a} and {b}, two separate collectors.
explained.tdh.how.identity.caption: Wallet A holds most of a season and wallet B the rest. Linked, the identity holds the whole season and one boost of {boost} lies across everything; apart, neither has a boost. Example wallets, real rates.
explained.tdh.how.n.label: The network
explained.tdh.how.n.title: Today's total is the sum of {identities} identities.
explained.tdh.how.n.bodyMore: Every identity's TDH, added up, is the network's: {total} in the result dated {date}, {delta} more than the day before.
explained.tdh.how.n.bodyLess: Every identity's TDH, added up, is the network's: {total} in the result dated {date}, {delta} less than the day before.
explained.tdh.how.n.bodyTotal: Every identity's TDH, added up, is the network's: {total} in the result dated {date}.
explained.tdh.how.n.cutover: About {date}, 6529.io moves to computing TDH with the Rust core, the program the daily check compares it with today.
explained.tdh.how.n.cutoverPast: 6529.io's move to computing TDH with the Rust core was planned for about {date}; the daily check says which program its numbers match.
explained.tdh.how.n.unavailable: Today's totals could not be read from the daily comparison. The rules above do not depend on them.
explained.tdh.how.model.unavailable: This model needs the Meme editions from 6529.io, which could not be read just now.

explained.tdh.how.hwk.modelsBody: The TDH v1.4 engine, run in your browser. It passes all {pass} of P26's {vectors} vectors that are in its scope, rerun in CI on every change.
